trusted_writer: experiment supervisor and immutable evaluator; not participant
source_snapshot_rules: Freeze all production RTL, program generators, host code, adapters and constraints before evaluation.
Include required run-time instruction images and parameter tables in the manifest.
Do not count logs or rebuilt binary timestamps as source revisions.
Do not overwrite snapshots or failed reports.
The first submitted integration revision is repair zero, including compile or elaboration failure.
Increment repair count on a changed source manifest since the preceding submission.
Retries of unchanged source do not increment the repair count.
Record independent self-test and editing iterations separately; submission count is not total debugging effort.
checkpoint_reporting_rules: Report evaluated coverage and the full denominator of assigned runs, including timeouts.
Public evaluator results at a checkpoint are labelled public success, not hidden success.
Replay preserved snapshots after session end to obtain hidden success at earlier checkpoints.
Do not give hidden failure details to an active participant.
Record both first verified success within budget and the final submitted source result.
An earlier pass does not excuse a regression in the final submitted source.
Unavailable checkpoints remain unevaluated unless the same verified final source is explicitly carried forward after early success.
cycle_comparison_rule: Use identical inputs, memory latency, ready stalls and seed. Publish stall-free and stressed runs separately.
resource_comparison_rule: Compare fully linked tops at the same part, clock and memory implementation; account for ISA instruction memory. Report simulation memory models separately from synthesizable banks.
unassisted_success_rule: No design hints, human source edits or progress prompts after the initial specification.
evaluator_infrastructure_rule: Infrastructure failure is recorded and rerun on the same snapshot; it is never converted to a design PASS or silently discarded.
